target_moa.text: Leniolisib is a small molecule selective inhibitor of the PI3K delta catalytic subunit p110δ; overactive PI3Kδ drives APDS, and leniolisib inhibits the mutant enzyme and reduces pAKT pathway activity.

citations.quote: Leniolisib is a small molecule selective inhibitor of phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta (PI3K\delta) catalytic subunit p110\delta that converts phosphatidylinositol (4,5)-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) into phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5- triphosphate (PIP3), an important phospholipid that anchors and activates many downstream kinases. p110\delta is principally expressed in leukocytes. Overactive PI3K\delta c

Pharmacological studies demonstrated that leniolisib binds to the active site of PI3Kδ. In cell-free isolated enzyme assays, leniolisib was selective for PI3Kδ over PI3Kα (28-fold), PI3Kβ (43-fold), and PI3Kγ (257-fold), as well as the broader kinome. In cell-based assays, leniolisib reduced pAKT pathway activity and inhibited proliferation and activation of B and T cell subsets.

The Applicant has submitted an NDA for leniolisib, a small molecule inhibitor of p110\delta, for the treatment of APDS in patients age \ge 12 years. Efficacy and safety were supported by one adequate and well controlled 12-week, pivotal phase 3 trial (Trial 2201, Part 2), in a total of 31 adults and adolescents. summary.text: Leniolisib received a traditional (full) approval under a Priority review NDA, supported by one adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trial with confirmatory evidence. It had Orphan Drug Designation for APDS (granted January 30, 2018) and rare pediatric disease designation (August 26, 2020), and the approval conferred a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. It was the first product approved for APDS.
